newsitem.title: USA: Foreign holdings of US securities jump in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Foreign holdings of US securities jump in 1996.

text.p: Foreigners nearly doubled their purchases of marketable U.S. Treasury bonds and notes during 1996 from a year earlier, the Treasury Department said on Friday.
Foreign purchases of bonds and notes during all of 1996 totaled $244.17 billion compared with $134.12 billion during 1995, Treasury said in its quarterly Bulletin.

Part of the reason for lower 1995 purchases was that the government temporarily suspended sales of Treasury securities late that year amid a debt crisis as the Clinton administration and Congress wrangled over raising the debt limit.
